atomic_functions.name: validate_percent_zero
atomic_functions.purpose: Parse and validate the Coupon and Est. Yield percent fields on all three entry surfaces — candidate add, Move to Portfolio, Add Position (D41): trim the submitted string, match a non-negative numeric pattern that allows leading zeros, and accept zero — '00.00', '0.00', '0' all parse to the numeric value 0. Reject empty (missing or whitespace-only), garbage (any non-numeric content) and negative (below zero) with a named validation error naming the field and zero writes. One validator, three funnels: the exact same rule runs on every path, closing the D41 smoke finding where POST /watch 0.00 was rejected with 400.
inputs: raw Coupon string submitted by the candidate-add, Move to Portfolio or Add Position form
raw Est. Yield string submitted by the same three forms
parse rules: trim, non-negative numeric pattern with leading zeros allowed (00.00 -> 0)
outputs: normalized non-negative numeric value handed to the insert path — zero preserved as 0, never dropped or defaulted
named validation error naming the offending field on empty/garbage/negative, with zero writes
read-back value used by the caller to echo the accepted input on success
triggers: Move to Portfolio POST carrying coupon / est-yield
Add Position POST carrying coupon / est-yield
preconditions: The three forms expose Coupon and Est. Yield as submitted text/number inputs (D41 surfaces)
Error surfacing wrapper available (AF-30) for the named validation error
postconditions: '00.00', '0.00', '0' and normal positives all pass and are stored as parsed values — zero is a value, not an absence (FR-62)
Empty, whitespace-only, non-numeric ('abc', '12%') and negative ('-0.50') inputs are each rejected with a named error naming the field and ZERO writes on all three paths (FR-62)
An accepted zero renders unchanged on the Watchlist and Portfolio — never coerced to empty, never silently defaulted (FR-62)
Identical payloads produce identical verdicts on candidate add, move and add — no path applies a looser or stricter rule (FR-62, D41)
Rejection surfaces visibly with the field named — never a silent no-op (FR-21)
Validation runs BEFORE any insert step: a rejected percent field leaves every table untouched (FR-64 validation-before-insert rule)

atomic_functions.name: validate_move_inputs
atomic_functions.purpose: Move-path insert validation parity with /add (D41): before the Move to Portfolio write runs, execute the same field rules Add Position runs — dates parseable with end after start, computed tenure at least 1 whole month (AF-50 arithmetic), credit day an integer in 1..31, amount numeric and non-negative, percent fields through AF-70 — and reject any violation with HTTP 400 plus a named error naming the offending field, writing zero rows. This is the guard whose absence let the D41 tenure-0 row in (MCP row id=2, start 2026-11-14, end 2026-11-30, inserted with a 302) and later 500'd on /, /portfolio, payouts and /print.
inputs: move payload: amount, start_date, end_date, credit_day, coupon, est-yield (fields a candidate may lack)
computed tenure_months = whole months between start_date and end_date (AF-50 date_range_tenure arithmetic)
credit_day bound: integer 1..31 (0, 32 and non-integers rejected — same bound as /add per FR-54)
the /add validation rule set itself, as the parity target
outputs: validated field set handed to the move write step (AF-66 watch_state flip)
on any violation: HTTP 400 with a named error naming the field and ZERO writes — no position row, no watch_state change, no ledger row
read-back echo of the validated values so the form can re-render the user's input on rejection
triggers: Move to Portfolio POST reaching the insert step
API-level move POST for a watching row
preconditions: Date/tenure validator available (AF-50) for the whole-month tenure arithmetic
Error surfacing wrapper available (AF-30) for the named 400 response
postconditions: TENURE >= 1: start 2026-11-14 with end 2026-11-30 computes tenure 0 and is rejected with HTTP 400 naming the dates/tenure field — the exact D41 row shape can never be written again (FR-64)
CREDIT BOUNDS: credit_day 0, 32 or a non-integer is rejected with HTTP 400 naming the field — the identical outcome /add produces for the identical payload (FR-64)
DATE RULES: unparseable dates or end_date not after start_date raise a named error naming the field (FR-64)
PARITY: any payload rejected by /add is rejected here and any payload accepted by /add is accepted here — one rule set, two funnels, identical verdicts (FR-64)

VALIDATION BEFORE INSERT: all checks complete before the write begins — on rejection zero rows are written or updated, so no partial writes (position row, watch_state flip and ledger rows all untouched) (FR-64, D41)
The rejection is a plain HTTP 400 with a named error — never a success-shaped 302 redirect (the failure mode that hid the D41 tenure-0 insert) (FR-64, D41)
On pass, validation itself writes nothing — only the downstream AF-66 write step changes the row (separation of concerns)

atomic_functions.name: render_health_safe
atomic_functions.purpose: Per-row render guard (D41): isolate each row's rendering and health/query derivation inside a per-row try/catch so one bad row — unparseable dates, tenure 0, non-numeric amount — can never abort a page. The failing row renders as an 'Invalid' chip carrying a Remove action, every other row renders normally, and the page returns HTTP 200. Applies to the four surfaces that 500'd in the D41 evidence — Dashboard (/), Portfolio (/portfolio), the payouts grid and /print (ERR-health-compute, ERR-query-counts, ERR-print-statement) — and to any other row-rendering surface.
inputs: row set fetched for the page (positions, candidates or payout rows)
per-row derivation work: health compute, query counts, print statement assembly
row-level fault raised while processing one row (unparseable dates, tenure 0, non-numeric amount)
outputs: page payload with every row represented: good rows rendered normally, the failing row carrying an 'Invalid' chip and a Remove action targeting its id
HTTP 200 for the page whenever row data is the only fault
page-level fault (database unreachable, broken template) still raised as a named error via AF-30 — never swallowed
triggers: render of Dashboard (/), Portfolio (/portfolio), the payouts grid and /print
render of any other surface that lists rows (Watchlist, drawer fragment)
any read that derives health or counts per row after a bad row lands in the database
preconditions: Error surfacing wrapper available (AF-30) for genuine page-level failures
Row loops structured so one row's exception is catchable without aborting the loop
postconditions: HTTP 200 GUARANTEED: with any single bad row present, /, /portfolio, payouts and /print each return 200 — the ERR-health-compute, ERR-query-counts and ERR-print-statement 500s are impossible (FR-65)
The bad row renders with the exact chip label 'Invalid' plus a Remove action bound to that row's id; all other rows render with their normal content (FR-65)
Multiple bad rows degrade independently — each failing row shows its own chip, none suppresses the others or the healthy rows (FR-65)
The guard isolates ROW faults only: infrastructure faults (database unreachable) still surface as named errors — it never masks a real outage (FR-21)
Render is read-only: the guard never rewrites, clamps or deletes row data while recovering — recovery is presentation only (DATA-05, D41)
The 'Invalid' chip never leaks raw exception text or stack details into the page — only the chip label and the Remove action (FR-21)

atomic_functions.name: remove_invalid_position
atomic_functions.purpose: Remove action behind the Invalid chip (D41): on POST of a row's Remove action, re-validate server-side — the id must exist and must target a bonds position row — then delete exactly that row together with its own ledger entries. Unknown, already-removed or non-position ids raise a named state error with zero writes. The client's claim that a row is invalid is never trusted as authorization; the server re-checks at delete time.
inputs: row id posted by the Remove action on an Invalid chip
server-side existence check: does this id exist on bonds?
server-side type check: does this id target a position row (not an arbitrary table)?
outputs: exactly one position row deleted on pass, with its own ledger entries removed alongside it
named state error with zero writes on fail (unknown id, already removed, wrong row type)
the surface re-renders without the removed row; remaining rows keep their own render state
triggers: user clicks Remove on an Invalid chip row (Dashboard, Portfolio, payouts or print-rendered list)
API-level removal POST for a row id
preconditions: AF-72 rendered the Invalid chip and bound the Remove action to the row id
postconditions: SERVER-SIDE RE-VALIDATION: existence and row type are re-checked at delete time — a stale or forged id is rejected with a named state error and zero writes (FR-65)
Exactly one position row is deleted on pass; a change count of 0 (unknown or already-removed id) raises the named state error instead of succeeding silently (FR-65)
The removed position's own ledger entries are removed with it, so no orphaned payment rows survive the deletion (FR-65)
No other row is touched — positions, candidates and ledger rows belonging to other ids are never modified by a removal (FR-65)
Removal is idempotent-safe: the second removal of the same id is a named state error with zero writes, not a second success (FR-21)
Removal never runs through the render guard's catch block as a side effect — it is an explicit user action with its own validation, never an automatic cleanup (D41)
A blocked removal surfaces visibly with the reason named — never a silent no-op (FR-21)

atomic_functions.name: broker_persist
atomic_functions.purpose: Persist and surface the broker detail field across its five surfaces (D41 broker provenance): ALTER bonds with a nullable TEXT broker column; write it from the candidate-add form, the Move to Portfolio form and the Add Position form; read it into the Watchlist Broker column and the Portfolio holdings detail drawer. Move carries the candidate's stored broker value onto the holding unchanged (roundtrip candidate -> holding); an explicit edit on the move form replaces it. NULL is the natural absent state and renders blank — never the string 'null'. Free-text offline input only: no broker integration, no network lookup (D33).
inputs: broker free-text string from the candidate-add, Move to Portfolio or Add Position form (optional)
bonds.broker column — nullable TEXT (schema from AF-01 migration)
stored broker value on a candidate row at move time (for the candidate -> holding roundtrip)
row payloads for the Watchlist column and the holdings drawer reads
outputs: bonds.broker written as the submitted text, or NULL when the input is absent or empty (no fabricated default, no '' sentinel)
on move: the holding's broker equals the candidate's stored broker unless the move form explicitly replaced it
watchlist row payload carrying broker for the Broker column
holdings drawer payload carrying broker for display
triggers: Move to Portfolio POST with broker input
Add Position POST with broker input
preconditions: Schema initialized (AF-01) including the nullable TEXT broker column (ALTER bonds, no new table)
postconditions: COLUMN EXISTS AS TEXT NULL: inserts with no broker value store NULL; an empty submitted input stores NULL — never an empty-string sentinel and never a fabricated default (FR-66)
FIVE SURFACES: value saved on the candidate form appears in the Watchlist Broker column; the move form and add form each capture and store it; the holdings drawer displays the stored value (FR-66)
ROUNDTRIP: broker 'Example Securities' saved on a candidate reads back identical after Move to Portfolio — same string, no truncation, no reformatting (FR-66, D41)
NULL RENDERS BLANK: a row with broker NULL shows an empty cell in both the Watchlist column and the drawer — the string 'null' never appears (FR-66)
The field is never populated by an integration or network call — offline manual text only (D33, D41)
Validation is format-free: any non-empty text is stored as given; the field never blocks an otherwise valid insert and never raises over free text (FR-21)
Writes happen only on the three form POSTs — rendering the Watchlist column or the drawer performs no write (DATA-05)

change_record: addendum v5.0 extends Atomic_Functions_addendum_v4 after owner decision D41 (CONFIRMED post-launch patch wave of 2026-11-01: zero-value percent allowance, explicit date labels, move-path validation parity, invalid-row render recovery, broker detail field); adds AF-70..AF-74 covering FR-62..FR-66, the five ids of docs/PRD_DK_Bond_Tracker_addendum_v5.json / docs/SRS_DK_Bond_Tracker_addendum_v5.json. D41 evidence carried into the design: smoke POST /watch 0.00 -> 400 (AF-70 target), unlabeled move dates from the owner screenshot (FR-63 labels on the AF-65/AF-66 forms), tenure-0 row via move with a 302 insert (MCP row id=2, start 2026-11-14, end 2026-11-30, tenure 0) then 500 on four surfaces — /, /portfolio, payouts, /print — with ERR-health-compute / ERR-query-counts / ERR-print-statement (AF-71 + AF-72 target), and the broker provenance requirement (AF-74). Coverage judgements (all 5 keys non-empty): FR-62 maps to AF-70 alone — one validator owns the parse rule on all three entry paths; FR-63 (exact form labels) is static template chrome, mapped to the two form-owning handlers AF-65 (add_position) and AF-66 (move_to_portfolio) exactly as v4 mapped the static sidebar labels of FR-51 to their only serving handler — no label-rendering AF is needed; FR-64 maps to the parity validator AF-71 plus its enforcing funnel AF-66 (AF-65 is the parity target, not the changed path); FR-65 maps to AF-72 (render recovery) and AF-73 (the Remove action the chip exposes); FR-66 maps to AF-74 (schema + three form writes) plus the existing read surfaces AF-52 (Watchlist read model carries the Broker column) and AF-54 (holdings drawer carries the display). Element notes: this wave introduces one element tag — render_guard (AF-72, per-row fault isolation at render time across Dashboard/Portfolio/payouts/print, distinct from month_grid_renderer which owns grid structure); AF-70 and AF-71 join validators beside AF-50, AF-73 and AF-74 are route_handlers. AF-71 depends_on AF-50 (tenure arithmetic), AF-70 (percent rules) and AF-30; AF-74 depends_on AF-01 (the bonds schema it ALTERs). Supersession/alignment: no v4 AF is edited or renumbered — AF-66 keeps its shared-lock semantics and ERR-move-watching shape; AF-71 ADDS the pre-write validation AF-66's brief lacked (tenure >= 1, credit bounds, named 400, no partial writes) without replacing the D15 lock, which still runs as its own step (AF-39); credit bounds stay 1..31 per FR-54 and the approved design, consistent with AF-65; AF-70 widens the percent parse to accept zero while keeping the empty/garbage/negative rejections — the D41 override of the smoke 400; AF-72's guard is presentation-only and never writes (DATA-05), and AF-73 is the single destructive path, gated on server-side re-validation per D41. Zero new tables: one nullable TEXT column (bonds.broker) is the entire schema delta. Alignment with parallel deliverables: docs/PRD_DK_Bond_Tracker_addendum_v5.json and docs/SRS_DK_Bond_Tracker_addendum_v5.json landed as the brief-31 siblings and were cross-checked id-for-id (FR-62..FR-66 semantics match: percent parse, exact label strings, parity 400/no-partial-writes, Invalid chip + Remove with HTTP 200, broker TEXT nullable with candidate -> holding roundtrip); docs/Test_Plan_addendum_v4.json (TC-105..TC-113) and docs/Development_Order_addendum_v4.json cover the v4 wave and are untouched — D41 test ids belong to a later test addendum. AF-01..AF-69 and all earlier coverage_map entries remain owned by their source documents and are unaltered.
